campaign.title: Aurelia 1978 launch campaign and Logix Computer Academy
campaign.objective: Communicate the launch, qualify demonstrations and coordinate follow-up described by the source campaign.
message: positioning / tagline: Logix Aurelia—a computer like no other. Your personal assistant in business.
positioning / academy message: Learn before you decide.
positioning / audience: Nontechnical business owners and managers; secondary audiences are dealers, software developers and peripheral manufacturers.

positioning / partner message: Business Tools organise office work; Abacus supports planning; independent BPI Systems maintains business records. Logix supplies the computer, not ownership of every application.
tagline: Logix Aurelia—a computer like no other. Your personal assistant in business.

activity.description: period: 1978-04; activity: Newspaper and business-press teasers introduce Aurelia and the personal-assistant promise; coming this spring, followed by June 5 launch date; brochure and invitation requests.
period: 1978-05; activity: Cinematic TV commercial and explanatory print advertisements; prioritise markets with demonstration, support and Academy coverage.
period: Late May to early June 1978; activity: Press previews, dealer/staff preparation, launch invitations, television-station outreach and complete venue rehearsal.
period: 1978-06-05; activity: NCC premiere in Anaheim, five-city Academy announcement, package and availability presentation, registration and ordering.
period: 1978-06-05 to 1978-06-08; activity: Technical sessions, repeated hands-on demonstrations, professional recording of every Logix NCC presentation and Academy registration.

period: After NCC, June 1978 onward; activity: Edit and freely distribute television packages; run Academy courses and dealer demonstrations; advertise practical business uses, real package prices, local dates and documented customer experience as it becomes available.

period: 1978-03-20; activity: Target 10–15 pilot businesses and several accounting practices; reconcile results against existing records. Validate representative data volumes, disk/RAM budgets, posting, corrections, backup/restore and supported payroll jurisdictions before launch claims.

period: 1978-05-15; activity: Qualify all advertised launch modules and a modest summary export to Abacus. Train instructors and dealers, publish requirements and support boundaries, and prepare a joint press preview. Measured capacity and final jurisdiction coverage remain acceptance gates, not invented results.

period: 1978-07-17; activity: Begin BPI dealer qualification and accountant demonstration access, permission-based case studies and defined paid setup assistance. Each initial Academy centre has access to a BPI specialist; recruit or train ahead of demand.

period: 1978-10-16; activity: Run year-end preparation workshops and module-upgrade demonstrations. Specify payroll update coverage and maintenance terms. Customer data remains under customer control; referrals do not imply an accountant endorsement without consent.

period: 1979-01-15; activity: Expand demonstrations and qualified support using verified customer results. Promote module-to-suite upgrade credit. BPI Model II support is a separate future negotiation; the existing Tandy agreement covers Abacus only.

television commercial / format: Proposed 60-second film-trailer-style advertisement; final 10–15 seconds show Aurelia, Abacus, a printed result, logo and June 5 premiere date. Include a recognisable BPI report with its own branding; detailed accounting explanation belongs in print and follow-up films.
television commercial / proposed lead: Michael Douglas
television commercial / casting status: Fictional casting proposal; availability, fee and contract not established.

television commercial / story: Narrator introduces This spring. Douglas discusses a remarkably helpful new assistant during a therapy session. The reveal identifies Aurelia as a computer, and the therapist becomes curious about a demonstration.
television commercial / tone: Warm humour, concrete business benefits and consistent interaction; avoid unhealthy dependency or claims of speech recognition/artificial intelligence.
television commercial / conversion: Telephone enquiries, mailed brochures, demo appointments and Academy bookings; trained staff handle responses.
premiere / date: 1978-06-05
premiere / venue: Booked auditorium or negotiated NCC presentation slot in Anaheim; access to a main stage is not assumed.
premiere / duration minutes before questions: 44
premiere / stages / 0 / id: opening
premiere / stages / 0 / minutes: 3

premiere / stages / 0 / description: Adam introduces almost four years of development toward an accessible, dependable business assistant; acknowledges the assembled personal computers popularised in 1977.
premiere / stages / 1 / id: reveal
premiere / stages / 1 / minutes: 3

premiere / stages / 1 / description: Reveal one Aurelia platform with detachable keyboard and two display choices. Power on colour and 16-shade grayscale systems and show startup; no claim of two different CPU models.
premiere / stages / 2 / id: editing
premiere / stages / 2 / minutes: 5
premiere / stages / 2 / description: Prepare a customer quotation letter, demonstrate consistent editing and the copy-buffer; explain how learning transfers between applications.
premiere / stages / 3 / id: peripherals
premiere / stages / 3 / minutes: 3

premiere / stages / 3 / description: Attach the self-powered printer at a safely quiescent FlexiBUS port with Aurelia powered on, wait for identification, and print. Once the job finishes, safely interchange printer and keyboard ports and verify both. No removal during traffic or unrestricted hot-plug claim.
premiere / stages / 4 / id: business_tools
premiere / stages / 4 / minutes: 3
premiere / stages / 4 / description: Use address book, calendar and calculator in the same customer-order workflow.
premiere / stages / 5 / id: abacus
premiere / stages / 5 / minutes: 8

premiere / stages / 5 / description: Safely attach external FDD, load Abacus from diskette, explain a small worksheet, then open a 500-plus-row business document. Raise supplier costs by 8%, show automatic recalculation, add and fill a column using IF to flag low-margin orders, print a short report, save, close and reopen. Use readable worksheet sections on 320x200 launch displays. Use a labelled prepared worksheet with BPI-exported totals; explain their origin. The following BPI demonstration shows the source records and export. Rehearse the shorter slot; retain the full workload for hands-on sessions.
premiere / stages / 6 / id: bpi
premiere / stages / 6 / minutes: 7

premiere / stages / 6 / description: Independent BPI Systems demonstrates a small wholesaler: existing customer/invoice records, incoming payment and remaining balance, receivables/payables and a concise report, then summary export for Abacus. Prepared history is labelled. No live write-back or simultaneous applications. Software presenter explains the workflow; the BPI head speaks in the subsequent partners section.
premiere / stages / 7 / id: partners
premiere / stages / 7 / minutes: 7

premiere / stages / 7 / description: Gary explains independent CP/M OEM availability, published interfaces and optional extensions; CP/M, hardware and application licenses remain distinct. MPI explains the printer partnership and any separately agreed future FlexiBUS devices. Do not announce the later July SMC agreement. The head of BPI Systems explains its independent brand, management, software ownership and support, with AION/Logix cooperation and Adam’s uncompleted investment offer disclosed. No invented name or claim of unrelated ownership.
premiere / stages / 8 / id: academy
premiere / stages / 8 / minutes: 2

premiere / stages / 8 / description: Announce Logix Computer Academy in five US cities: learn before you decide, hands-on Fundamentals, configuration advice, 50% tuition purchase credit and direct ordering. Show selected locations, first course dates and exact tuition once finalised. BPI-authorised courses start June 12; specialist support is provided by BPI.
premiere / stages / 9 / id: packages
premiere / stages / 9 / minutes: 3

premiere / stages / 9 / description: State complete package contents and prices, delivery dates, warranty, training and service; invite orders, Academy registration and dealer demonstrations; announce the two technical sessions. Show optional dealer-assembled BPI configurations, separate supplier licences and training/setup prices.
premiere / questions: Moderated questions follow the presentation.
premiere / display: Colour and grayscale launch monitor options; readable 320x200 worksheet sections, not an implied 80-column or whole-document display.

academy / credit / accounting: Reserve the redeemed credit once as promotional expense across the course and computer sale, outside recurring manufacturing costs.

academy / bpi support: Access to a BPI specialist at each launch centre; authorised curriculum and escalation agreement. Training, setup and software licensing are separate; no automatic Fundamentals credit for BPI courses.
broadcast program / scope: Every Logix presentation at NCC 1978, including the premiere, both technical sessions, partner appearances, questions and any additional Logix sessions.

broadcast program / production: Professional multi-camera crew with clean presenter audio, audience/reaction coverage and close-ups of the computer, screen, connections and printouts. Retain full-session recordings and production masters.
broadcast program / deliverables / 0: Attractively edited broadcast feature with a clear business-user narrative
broadcast program / deliverables / 1: Short station-ready news packages and demonstration excerpts
broadcast program / deliverables / 2: Clean footage, separate narration/audio where practical, accurate captions and a factual product/Academy press sheet
broadcast program / deliverables / 3: Full edited presentations for stations wanting longer technical coverage

broadcast program / distribution: Offer and supply the material free of charge to any television station wishing to broadcast it; Logix covers normal duplication and dispatch. Supply station-compatible broadcast copies on request.
broadcast program / broadcast fee usd: 0

broadcast program / editorial policy: Station participation, scheduling and editorial selection are voluntary; no guaranteed airtime, compulsory advertising purchase or claimed editorial endorsement. Identify the material as supplied by Logix.

broadcast program / rights: Arrange presenter, partner, music and production rights covering free television redistribution before recording. Michael Douglas commercial footage may be included only if separately cleared for this use.

broadcast program / fidelity: Do not accelerate startup or recalculation, conceal failures through misleading cuts, or present pre-recorded footage as a live result. Identify edited excerpts and show only qualified claims.

broadcast program / timing: Record throughout June 5–8; begin station outreach before NCC and distribute edited packages after the conference as edits and broadcast clearances are completed. Exact delivery dates and runtime remain production decisions.

broadcast program / engineering: Qualify a custom Aurelia digital-video-to-projection/recording path; rehearse readability, lighting and sound in the hired room. Use a backup demonstration system and clearly identified recorded fallback.

business sessions / 0 / duration minutes range / 1: 45

Post-NCC 1978 recording, editing and television distribution

acceptance gates / 3: Confirm celebrity/partner contracts, venue, Academy cities/course dates, tuition, product packages, delivery, warranty and service before publishing definitive claims.
acceptance gates / 4: Measured 48 KB workspace, disk capacity and supported disk configuration; 64 KB or extra drives only when qualified and separately quoted.
acceptance gates / 5: Posting consistency, correction history, disk-full handling and tested backup/restore.
acceptance gates / 6: Readable reports on launch display and supported printers; supported forms and paper documented.
acceptance gates / 7: Payroll jurisdictions, update process and maintenance responsibility explicitly documented.
acceptance gates / 8: Qualify BPI summary export and Abacus import; demonstrate actual sequential applications and label prepared data.

campaign.title: NCC 1979 open architecture and migration campaign
campaign.objective: Recruit independent computer, software and peripheral manufacturers to the published compatibility programmes, and help existing customers carry their applications and documents across supported systems.
message: positioning / message: Choose your computer. Keep your investment.
positioning / openness: Documented interfaces, non-exclusive implementation rights and predictable commercial access; CP/M remains commercially licensed, not automatically free or open-source.

activity.description: profiles / 0 / id: cpm_application
profiles / 0 / name: CP/M application compatibility
profiles / 0 / required: Named OS core version, optional extension version, ISA, TPA/resource budget, adapters and qualified application editions; common document formats and documented APIs.
profiles / 0 / optional: FlexiBUS and Logix video; native host display, disks and conventional ports remain valid.
profiles / 0 / limits: Standard CP/M availability does not guarantee every extended application, Z80-only binary, file system or floppy format.
profiles / 1 / id: flexibus_peripheral
profiles / 1 / name: FlexiBUS peripheral compatibility
profiles / 1 / required: Published electrical/transport rules plus device-class profile, host driver, diagnostics and named qualification.
profiles / 1 / optional: CP/M and Logix video; other OS/CPU hosts can implement their own drivers.

profiles / 1 / limits: Identification is not feature compatibility. V1 is one device per point-to-point host port, no implied passive hub or daisy chain; faster rate permits at most 50 KB/s before protocol overhead.
profiles / 2 / id: logix_display
profiles / 2 / name: Logix display compatibility
profiles / 2 / required: Distinguish software API conformance from optional controller/card, digital link and qualified monitor modes.
profiles / 2 / optional: FlexiBUS and adoption of the full Aurelia architecture.
profiles / 2 / limits: 80-column display requires a qualified 640-pixel monitor; existing 320-pixel launch monitors do not gain it from a card alone.

date: 1979-02-19; activity: Begin confidential briefings and engineering-kit evaluations. Prioritise North Star and Vector Graphic as prospects; approach Cromemco, Altos, Intertec and Heath selectively. Invitations are not signed agreements or qualified products.

date: 1979-05-05; activity: Alongside the existing DRI portable-extension release, publish separate CP/M application, FlexiBUS peripheral and optional Logix display compatibility profiles, reference-driver and test access, non-exclusive implementation principles and support-roadmap requirements. Exact fees and support duration remain to be settled.

date: 1979-05-21; activity: Invite computer, software and peripheral suppliers to test named configurations and document failures before public demonstrations. Supplier attendance and passing results must be verified; no announcement of an unsigned OEM.

date: 1979-06-04; activity: Present a 50-minute cross-vendor campaign before questions. Demonstrate applications/documents, then independent BPI, FlexiBUS, Apple native drivers and optional video. BPI management speaks with partners. State that the next generation breaks native Z80 binary compatibility; C source/API portability reduces migration work and a planned optional Z80 compatibility coprocessor supports qualified legacy software. Reveal neither processor word size nor architecture before NCC 1980. See ncc_1979_campaign.json.

date: 1979-07-16; activity: Run dealer demonstrations, joint trade-press activity and developer clinics. Teach documented APIs, file interchange, C portability boundaries and device-class drivers. Publish a directory distinguishing shipping, qualified and prototype configurations.

date: 1979-10-15; activity: Promote the separately recorded Tandy customer release and only individually qualified SMC or peripheral products. Update directory evidence; do not imply all licensed chips, every peripheral class or new independent OEM systems are shipping.

date: 1979-12-15; activity: Target Tandy shipping, one additional named OEM selling a supported CP/M-extension/FlexiBUS option, another OEM in qualification, dealer/integrator configurations and third-party devices in several categories. These are adoption targets, not recorded achievements or contracted orders.

date: 1980-01-14; activity: Publish verified customer examples, compatibility results and partner configurations. Target three to five non-Logix manufacturers with supported configurations by NCC 1980, counting Tandy once and excluding duplicate dealer builds. Do not disclose the new processor architecture early.

premiere / stages / 6 / id: migration
premiere / stages / 6 / minutes: 5

premiere / stages / 6 / description: Adam states that the next generation will break native Z80 binary compatibility. Existing C tools and documented APIs reduce source migration effort; recompilation, adaptation and testing remain necessary. A planned optional Z80 coprocessor offers qualified legacy execution. Architecture and word size remain secret until NCC 1980. Eight-bit systems retain business uses and broaden into homes and education as prices fall. Adam forecasts that next-generation computers using an existing television and basic storage will remain above roughly $100 for about a decade; this is a strategic expectation, not a withdrawal date or price guarantee.

migration / disclosure: Public 1979 materials withhold word size, ISA details and architecture; full project technical catalog is an author-facing specification, not a 1979 press kit.
migration / native binary compatibility: false

migration / source path: Use the existing Z80 C environment, documented APIs, portable file formats and separated platform adapters. Recompile for the later target; review assembly, integer/pointer assumptions, memory banking and direct hardware access.

migration / legacy path: Planned optional Z80 coprocessor for qualified legacy applications. Implementation details remain confidential; this is not a universal guarantee for hardware-dependent software.
migration / public status: Future commitment, not a shipping or fully qualified June-1979 product.
migration / support: Maintain CP/M tools and applications alongside next-generation development; publish a funded duration before making a dated service guarantee.

disclosure policy / scope: Every 1979 keynote, Q&A, press release, advertisement, dealer script, sales proposal, partner/OEM briefing, roadshow, developer clinic and demonstration. Confidential internal engineering is not a public announcement.
disclosure policy / public name: next-generation computers
disclosure policy / permitted / 0: Native binary compatibility with existing Z80 applications will break.
disclosure policy / permitted / 1: The established C development environment and documented interfaces will minimise source migration effort; adaptation, recompilation and testing remain necessary.
disclosure policy / permitted / 2: An optional Z80 coprocessor is planned for qualified legacy applications; availability and compatibility are not guaranteed for every model.

disclosure policy / withheld / 3: Coprocessor implementation, interconnect, memory mapping and host integration.
disclosure policy / withheld / 4: Future-target SDKs, compiler output, binaries, benchmarks and demonstrations that allow architectural inference.

disclosure policy / enforcement: Use only released 8-bit products in 1979 demonstrations and clinics. Review slides, screenshots, captions, attachments and linked specifications as well as speech. Do not attach the all-years technical catalog or disclose future implementation details to prospective partners; current CP/M, FlexiBUS and optional video specifications remain available.

compatibility policy / scope: Released Artemis application binaries using documented, supported ERA/AIONix interfaces retain a supported execution path on subsequent Logix professional platforms through 2000: native execution, a maintained compatibility runtime, or emulation. Source portability is a separate commitment, not a substitute for the binary execution path.

compatibility policy / exclusions: Undocumented hardware access, unqualified peripherals and unsupported interfaces; no promise of unchanged speed, unlimited memory, or every future device. Z80 programs use their separately qualified compatibility path.

compatibility policy / delivery requirements: Publish versioned ABI/API eligibility and conformance tests; preserve reference binaries and regression workloads; budget compatibility engineering, runtime distribution and support. compatibility policy / status: Official scenario commitment at NCC 1980; future fulfilment is not established evidence.

claims / memory: Beyond the 64 KB application barrier; demonstrate a measured resident workload on a named 128 KB or 256 KB configuration. Finite RAM and process limits remain; no demand paging promised.

claims / os: Professional multitasking AIONix with Unix V7-inspired behaviour and familiar Logix TUI/keyboard conventions. Do not claim a Unix source licence or trademark endorsement without an established agreement.

claims / compiler: Artemis-hosted AION C IDE supplies ERA native and Z80 cross-compilers, target libraries and separate executables. Portable code following guidelines can require small changes; quantify changes for each demonstration rather than promising zero work.

claims / applications: Native Abacus 2, Business Tools and qualified independent BPI editions. Pulse 1 remains Aurelia+ software; a card demonstration requires guest OS/memory qualification. Native Pulse 3 and Abacus 3 launch only at COMDEX on November 19.
claims / continuity: Aurelia+ remains a supported value option; compatible independent 8-bit computers grow the ecosystem. No forced migration or promise that cheaper 8-bit demand disappears.
